title: Speed Reducer

introduction.definition: A speed reducer is an enclosed gear drive that lowers speed and raises torque. In this two-stage helical reducer, each stage's ratio equals its tooth ratio (32/16 and 45/15), giving 6:1 overall; output torque ≈ input torque × ratio × efficiency.
applications: Pump and fan drives at low speed
introduction.summary: A speed reducer (gearbox) lowers speed and raises torque between a motor and a slow machine. In this two-stage helical reducer, a 16-tooth pinion drives a 32-tooth gear (2:1), and a 15-tooth pinion on the same intermediate shaft drives a 45-tooth gear (3:1) — 6:1 overall. Helical teeth run quietly and carry high loads; the gears dip into an oil bath for lubrication.

foundation: Rigid, flat mounting; shim to avoid housing distortion.
alignment: Align shafts parallel and the wheels/hubs in the same plane (straight-edge or laser); misalignment is the main cause of early wear.
piping: Fit guards that fully enclose moving parts but allow inspection and lubrication.
commissioning: Check rotation, set tension/slack or torque setting, run in and re-check after the first hours of operation.

routine.task: Check oil level, temperature and noise.

overhaul.task: Replace bearings and seals; inspect tooth contact.

lubrication: Gear oil grade per AGMA 9005 / maker (ISO VG 150–460 typical).

video_tutorials.title: Speed Reducer — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Speed Reducer.
A speed reducer is an enclosed gear drive that lowers speed and raises torque.
In this two-stage helical reducer, each stage's ratio equals its tooth ratio (32/16 and 45/15), giving 6:1 overall; output torque ≈ input torque × ratio × efficiency.
Typical applications include conveyors, mixers, agitators; cranes and hoists; pump and fan drives at low speed; extruders and mills.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Gear Housing (split, front half removed in cutaway), Input Shaft & Pinion (z = 16), Intermediate Shaft: Gear (z = 32) & Pinion (z = 15), Output Shaft & Gear (z = 45).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Speed Reducer works.
The motor drives the input shaft and pinion at high speed.
The pinion turns the larger gear — first reduction (2:1).
The intermediate pinion drives the output gear — second reduction (3:1).
Gears dip into the oil bath, which lubricates gears and bearings by splash.
Bearings carry radial and helical axial loads.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Speed Reducer.
Check oil level, temperature and noise.
Change oil; oil analysis.
Clean breather.
Replace bearings and seals; inspect tooth contact.
Watch for tooth pitting / wear: noise, vibration, metal in oil. Common cause: overload, poor lubrication.
Watch for oil leakage: oil on base. Common cause: worn seals, blocked breather.
Watch for overheating: high oil temperature. Common cause: overload, wrong oil level.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
